Housing here runs to a median build year of 1965, and 76.9 percent of the 10,012 units in Burbank predate 1980. 2.1 percent are prewar. Age is the first thing worth knowing about a house before it gets quoted, and it is the thing most quotes skip.

Count it by household and Burbank is 7,761 owning against 1,913 renting, 80.2 percent owner occupied. Count it by building and it is 80.1 percent detached, 1.5 percent attached, 17.9 percent in twos or more. Median unit: 5.9 rooms. Median home value is $258,900.

Compared with the 76 place average behind this site, Burbank is unusual for prewar housing at 2.1 percent against a 15.8 percent average, townhomes and rowhouses at 1.5 percent against a 7.5 percent average and housing in buildings of two or more at 17.9 percent against a 29 percent average.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2019-2023 (tables B25003, B25024, B25034, B25035, B25077). Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

The part of a Burbank quote that actually varies

Housing built around 1965 is now on its second or third full repaint, which matters more than the first one did. Each earlier coat is a surface the new one has to bond to, and where the old work was done fast the new work has to undo it first. That is prep, it is most of the labor, and it is the honest reason two quotes for the same house can differ by a lot. The 7,761 to 1,913 split between owning and renting in Burbank means the same street can want two different things. A contractor who prices both the same way is wrong about one of them.

What an estimate here has to account for

  • Containment, not just paint. 76.9 percent of housing in Burbank was built before 1980, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Whole elevations. 80.1 percent of the housing is detached, so an exterior here is four sides and a garage rather than one face of a shared building.
  • Distance, stated. Burbank is 2.0 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Burbank is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is brick and brick-and-frame ranch and split-level. Exterior work in Burbank is fascia, soffit, gable ends and window trim, most of it off a ladder rather than off the ground.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1965 median build year, and the split between 80.1 percent detached houses, 1.5 percent attached homes and 17.9 percent in buildings of two units or more.

An inference, not a measurement. Neither the Census nor the regional housing data records what a wall in Burbank is made from, so no percentage is attached to it and none should be. Your own elevation settles it in four seconds from the sidewalk.

Burbank is mostly pre-1978 stock, and that changes the setup

The Census publishes a pre-1980 bucket rather than a pre-1978 one, and on that measure 76.9 percent of the housing sits on the older side of the line in Burbank. The federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule applies to work that disturbs paint in housing built before 1978, and in Illinois the EPA administers it directly rather than through a state program.

Read it as a method rather than a prohibition. Below roughly six square feet of disturbed paint in a room, or twenty outside, it does not bite. Above that, and on any window replacement in Burbank at all, it decides how the room is sealed and how it is left. On 5.9-room housing that threshold arrives early.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Burbank.

Ask about it early. It changes the sequence of a job rather than the price of the paint, and a contractor who has thought about it will tell you in plain terms what happens on day one.

No lead-safe certification is claimed anywhere on this site, because no number has been provided to put here. The panel below leaves the slot open on purpose, in Burbank and everywhere else. Ask any contractor for theirs.

Next door is not the same job

Put Burbank next to Bedford Park, 1.6 miles away, and the housing does not match. The gaps are owner households (7,761 against 161); share of units in buildings of two or more (17.9 percent against 2 percent); prewar share (2.1 percent against 42 percent).

Burbank is 2.0 straight-line miles from the shop, which puts it inside the ring where distance stops being a factor in what gets quoted.

For scale, the nearest other place on this site is Bedford Park, 1.6 miles from Burbank, and Burbank sits in Cook County.

The practical effect is scheduling. Small jobs fit into gaps in a week instead of waiting for a day that can absorb the driving, so you get a date sooner than the size of the job would suggest.

From the shop

Burbank is the largest of the genuinely old towns in the close ring, a median build year of 1965 across 10,012 housing units, and eight in ten households own their home. Almost all of that stock predates 1978, which puts it squarely inside the federal lead-safe renovation rule. That is not a scare line, it is a real difference in how an interior job gets set up, contained and cleaned, and it is worth asking any painter about before they start sanding your window casings.

Questions

Asked about Burbank

Is the $258,900 median home value in Burbank what a job here costs?

No. That figure describes the houses, not the work. $258,900 is what the Census estimates a home in Burbank is worth, and it earns its place on this page because value tracks size and age, which is what a painter is actually pricing. There is no price list on this site because there is no honest local one to publish yet.

Who actually shows up in Burbank?

Our crew, with Mike Walsh running it. He owns the company, and every job is quoted after we walk it. Tell us the town, the room and roughly what you want, and you will know what happens next on the same call. 708-935-4289.

Can it be done a room at a time?

It can. Splitting a 5.9-room house into phases is normal and it is priced as phases rather than as a discount on the whole. The trade-off is setup time, because masking and protecting a room costs the same whether it is one room or the fourth.

What changes the price most on a house here?

Condition, not size. On 1965-median stock in Burbank what varies is how much has to come off or be made good before anything goes on: loose paint, failed caulk, damaged trim, ceilings that have been patched before. Two houses on the same street can differ by a lot on that alone.
